<div class="sphinxpress-doc">
<section id="usage">
<h1>Usage</h1>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-initialize-workspace -->
<section id="initialize-a-workspace">
<h2>Initialize a workspace</h2>
<p>Run initialization from the repository root:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger init
</pre></div></div>
<p>By default this creates the canonical <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/</span></code> layout: <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/ledger.toml</span></code>, the Memoryledger tool configuration, and its project data mount. Use <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--project-name</span></code> to set the project name.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-check-workspace-status -->
</section>
<section id="check-workspace-status">
<h2>Check workspace status</h2>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger --json status
</pre></div></div>
<p>Status reports the workspace <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">state</span></code>:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">uninitialized</span></code>: no <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">memoryledger.toml</span></code> was found.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">bootstrap_required</span></code>: there is no baseline scan yet, or there is a baseline but no usable memory entries.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">incremental_clean</span></code>: the latest scan has no affected linked memory entries.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">incremental_affected</span></code>: the latest scan has affected linked memory entries that should be reviewed.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">mapping_incomplete</span></code>: changed evidence files are not yet fully linked to memory entries.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>The result also reports <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">recommended_command</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">recommended_reason</span></code>, compact latest-scan counts, and any root-layout diagnostics that should be fixed before trusting a baseline.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-run-scan -->
</section>
<section id="manage-memory-entries">
<h2>Manage memory entries</h2>
<p>Create and manage memory entries that capture agent knowledge:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger --json scan
</pre></div></div>
<p>A scan collects evidence files from the configured evidence roots, hashes them, indexes evidence units, and compares the current state to the previous scan. The first scan establishes a baseline and does not report changed, deleted, stale, or unlinked evidence.</p>
<p>Later scans report:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">unchanged</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">true</span></code> when the evidence and memory hashes match the previous scan exactly. No scan state is rewritten and the previous scan version is reused.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">changed_evidence</span></code>, evidence files whose hash changed or that are new since the previous scan.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">deleted_evidence</span></code>, evidence files that were present in the previous scan and are now gone.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">affected_entries</span></code>, the memory entries currently impacted by changed or deleted linked evidence.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">stale_memory</span></code>, a compatibility projection of the memory that still contains affected entries.</p></li>
<li><p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">unlinked_changed_evidence</span></code>, changed evidence files that do not have memory links.</p></li>
</ul>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-link-memory-to-sources -->
</section>
<section id="link-memory-to-sources">
<h2>Link memory to sources</h2>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger links add --entry memory/architecture.md --source src/core.py --reason "Records architecture decisions."
</pre></div></div>
<p>Whole-file links remain available as a broad fallback, but precise entry-level links are the default:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger links add-entry \
  --entry memory/api-design.md \
  --section api-design-endpoints \
  --evidence-unit py:function:src/api.py::create_endpoint \
  --coverage implementation \
  --impact behavior \
  --reason "Documents the endpoint creation logic."
</pre></div></div>
<p>Links use repository-relative POSIX paths. Entry paths must have configured memory extensions, evidence paths and evidence units must exist, and coverage and impact values are validated.</p>
<p>List and remove links with:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger links list
memledger links remove --entry memory/architecture.md --source src/core.py
memledger links remove-entry --entry memory/api-design.md --section api-design-endpoints --evidence-unit py:function:src/api.py::create_endpoint
</pre></div></div>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-find-and-update-stale-memory -->
</section>
<section id="find-and-update-stale-memory">
<h2>Find and update stale memory</h2>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger --json memory affected
memledger memory render-context --affected --out /tmp/memledger-context.md
</pre></div></div>
<p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">memory</span> <span class="pre">affected</span></code> reports the live affected entries for the latest scan. After an entry is updated and marked fresh, it disappears from <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">memory</span> <span class="pre">affected</span></code> immediately; a follow-up scan is optional confirmation, not the only way to clear affectedness.</p>
<p>The rendered context contains only the affected memory entries, their linked changed evidence units, the current relevant evidence snippets, unlinked changed evidence, and configured validation commands. Inspect the affected entries and linked changed evidence first. Expand to whole files only when the changed unit cannot be understood in isolation.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-render-memory-context -->
</section>
<section id="render-memory-context">
<h2>Render memory context</h2>
<p>Render context for agents to review and update memory:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger memory render-context --affected --print
memledger memory render-context --bootstrap --out /tmp/memledger-bootstrap.md
</pre></div></div>
<p>The rendered context provides agents with the information needed to update stale memory entries based on changed evidence.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-bootstrapping-a-new-repository -->
</section>
<section id="bootstrapping-a-new-repository">
<h2>Bootstrapping a new repository</h2>
<p>A fresh repository has no links yet, so the first scan reports no stale memory. To drive an initial memory pass, use the explicit bootstrap flow:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger init
memledger scan
memledger memory render-context --bootstrap --out /tmp/memledger-bootstrap.md
</pre></div></div>
<p>The bootstrap context gives agents a deterministic first-pass link graph without applying anything until the full batch validates. See <a class="reference internal" href="../bootstrap/"><span class="std std-doc">Bootstrap</span></a> for the full setup sequence.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-mark-memory-fresh -->
</section>
<section id="mark-memory-fresh">
<h2>Mark memory fresh</h2>
<p>After updating and validating an affected entry, mark it fresh:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger mark-fresh --entry memory/api-design.md --section api-design-endpoints --reason "Memory updated after scan version 2."
</pre></div></div>
<p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">mark-fresh</span></code> records the latest scan version, the current memory hash, the current entry hash, and the tracked evidence-unit hashes for the selected links. It requires a non-empty reason. Use <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--all</span></code> to mark every currently affected entry from the latest scan, or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--entry</span></code> without <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--section</span></code> to update all affected entries in one memory file explicitly.</p>
<p>Unlinked memory is rejected by default:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger mark-fresh --entry memory/index.md --reason "Navigation page."        # rejected: unlinked_memory
memledger mark-fresh --entry memory/index.md --allow-unlinked --reason "Navigation page."
</pre></div></div>
<p>This prevents silently tracking a memory that can never become stale from evidence changes. Pass <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--allow-unlinked</span></code> only for intentionally unlinked memory; the record stores the reason with an <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">(intentionally unlinked)</span></code> marker.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-validate-ledger-state -->
</section>
<section id="validate-ledger-state">
<h2>Validate ledger state</h2>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger doctor
</pre></div></div>
<p>Doctor checks storage schema metadata, memory record paths, suspicious root configuration, missing memory files, missing evidence files, duplicate edges, missing evidence-unit ids, and missing entry ids.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-json-and-human-output -->
</section>
<section id="json-and-human-output">
<h2>JSON and human output</h2>
<p>Pass <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--json</span></code> before the command to emit a stable JSON envelope:</p>
<div class="highlight-json notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">{</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"ok"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"command"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"status"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"result"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{},</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nt">"events"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">}</span>
</pre></div></div>
<p>Errors also use a JSON envelope when <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--json</span></code> is set, and the envelope preserves the real command name:</p>
<div class="highlight-json notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"ok"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"command"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"scan"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"error"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">{</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"code"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"workspace_not_found"</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"message"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"..."</span><span class="p">,</span>
<span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">"remediation"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[]</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="p">},</span>
<span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">"events"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[]</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</pre></div></div>
<p>Without <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--json</span></code>, commands print human-readable output and errors print concise <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Error:</span></code> messages with remediation hints.</p>
<!-- docledger-section: usage-ledger-state-and-commit-policy -->
</section>
<section id="ledger-state-and-commit-policy">
<h2>Ledger state and commit policy</h2>
<p>Memoryledger stores its durable state under <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/memoryledger/data/</span></code>; rendered and proposal artifacts use the resolved cache mount. The recommended commit policy for a memory management ledger is:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p>Commit <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/ledger.toml</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/memoryledger/config.toml</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/memoryledger/data/storage.yaml</span></code>, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/memoryledger/data/scan.yaml</span></code>, and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/memoryledger/data/memory/*.yaml</span></code>. These are the source of truth for project identity, the current scan baseline, entry-level links, tracked hash state, and freshness markers.</p></li>
<li><p>Ignore the resolved cache artifacts directory. Rendered context is regenerated on demand by <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">memory</span> <span class="pre">render-context</span></code>.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>Do not edit <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.ledger/</span></code> files directly; use the <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">memledger</span></code> commands so the records stay consistent.</p>
</section>
<section id="storage-commands">
<h2>Storage commands</h2>
<p>Use <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">memledger</span> <span class="pre">storage</span> <span class="pre">where</span></code> to inspect the active layout. Migrate a legacy workspace with a reviewed dry-run plan, then verify before any cleanup:</p>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>memledger storage migrate --dry-run --plan-file migration.json
memledger storage migrate --plan-file migration.json --adopt-project-uuid
memledger storage verify --strict
memledger storage cleanup-legacy --dry-run
</pre></div></div>
<p>Routine commands never migrate automatically and read-only commands do not initialize cache directories or repair bindings.</p>
</section>
</section>
</div>
